review.scope: Reviewed frozen working-tree bytes after the throughput/reliability revision. The base commit is the comparison baseline, not the modified runtime. Hashes are review tripwires, not a Rust/SQLite/Redis/filesystem refinement proof.
correspondence: NonceAllocator now models consumed-count floor with out-of-order retained receipt cleanup; separate bounded-page/RPC concurrency tests cover scheduling, not model throughput or fairness.

EOA Uncertain retains exact borrowed wire on all dispatch errors; same-identity retry stutters in EoaRecovery, included receipt only restores submitted projection. NOOP reserves submitted hash before dispatch; automatic NOOP reconciliation is not modeled or implemented.

DisasterRecovery terminal attribution requires the same admission independently executed its recorded attempt. Actual hash/signature/UserOperation computation and endpoint/genesis validation remain implementation checks.
Exact attempt and unchanged checkpoint no-ops retain health/owner/CAS guards; admission overload makes no durable transition. Retained terminal retries do not enqueue new work.
Solana independent signature reservation precedes Redis attempt storage; missing projection after SQL commit parks. The Redis and authority models are separate and not mechanically composed.

Bundled EIP-7702 is disabled and legacy work parks; no dedicated protocol qualification is claimed. Streaming export, HTTP authentication/semaphores and provider genesis checks are outside the state-machine proof.

progress_scheduling_followup.reason: Reviewed successful-cycle result construction: sent counts only moved-to-submitted acknowledgments, recovered counts submitted-projection reconciliation/acknowledgment, while uncertain attempts retain borrowed state. Only positive nondelegation plus unsigned backlog plus either positive progress counter skips delay and still rejoins queue tail. Delegated/unknown/no-progress/finality-only/error handling retain existing delays. EoaRecovery already admits transitions without wall-clock waits; QueueLease keeps fenced completion and pending membership. Timing, fairness, mixed-progress unknown-retry RPC costs and throughput remain outside these finite safety models. Real Redis regression exercises actual queue lease completion, tail ordering, ready work and rounded delayed scores.

depth_checkpoint_followup.status: Source correspondence reviewed and formatted candidate fingerprints recorded; implementation and TLC execution pending.
depth_checkpoint_followup.reason: The former Finality abstraction collapses heights and cannot detect persisting the observed tip above the probabilistic depth-qualified boundary. DepthCheckpoint now separates H, Q=H-depth, persisted anchor, independent canonical history and semantic qualified witness; tip-anchor and ignored-conflict mutations exercise distinct failures. Core and real-journal executor regressions retain within-assessment tip revalidation, allow shallow tip replacement, halt on qualified-boundary conflict, and preserve finalized/legacy conservative behavior. Monotonic journal CAS, multiple advancing checkpoints and composition remain outside this new single-checkpoint model.

gap_recovery_followup.status: Source reviewed after formatting and passing implementation suites; full model rerun recorded separately.
gap_recovery_followup.reason: The bounded getter reads an existing EOA attempt and rejects mismatched key/kind, terminal/quarantined admission or halted chain; it is not dispatch authorization. Replay decodes/re-encodes original EIP-2718 bytes, checks nonce/hash/sender/chain/attempt membership, rechecks owner and runs before_eoa again. No signing, fee change, replay-key mutation or terminal proof is added. Repeated original transmission collapses to stuttering in EoaRecovery/DisasterRecovery; sent is possible future delivery, not an evictable mempool. Retained cached consumed-count high-water supports the allocator floor, but NonceAllocator assumes monotonic chain consumption and does not model actual rollback. Fixed recovery windows, owner-fenced cooldown reservations, 32 sequential calls, missing-gap stop, actual counter progress and unchanged unknown-response behavior are implementation regression obligations, not newly proved scheduling/liveness properties. The 11-scenario real Redis/HTTP/SQLite parent test and broad executor/core suites passed; process reorg qualification remains separate. NOOP gaps and missing authoritative/projection data can stay unresolved.

reorg_oracle_followup.status: Source and existing passing implementation evidence reviewed; model rerun pending and not claimed by this metadata correction.
reorg_oracle_followup.reason: The strict process oracle now separates a retained attempt from transmissions: one unchanged durable wire must have an additional accepted Engine-only proxy send after the fault, then match the independently fetched signed transaction, canonical receipt/block, reserved nonce, outcome and delayed terminal proof. Terminal admission replay must add no send or attempt. The explicit legacy comparison option alone accepts an execution-equivalent fee replacement. Seven offline unittest methods include positive witnesses and adversarial evidence substitutions; their synthetic signatures do not verify cryptography. Normal and reverted real Anvil process cases passed against unchanged runtime binary a3d360eba3dc470bd830ec9d3a32e0be8e11b6764f9bbf6efeb319f080eb8515. Finality covers provisional versus terminal observations; EoaRecovery/DisasterRecovery cover retained identity and durable membership. Repeated identical dispatch is a stutter in the identity abstractions, not a new protocol transition. No model changes or new TLC cases are justified by this test-only oracle correction. Actual mempool eviction, timing, request pacing, node encoding and implementation/model composition remain outside those proofs. The capacity_faults.py mapping guards the shared raw-wire encoding and Engine-only accepted-send counter dependency; it does not claim formal coverage of the full capacity harness.

history_index_followup.status: Actual applied source matches independently reviewed draft; targeted implementation suites passed without source repairs; full model rerun recorded separately.
history_index_followup.reason: Nonunique (id,sequence) indexes change only physical lookup structure. Existing SQL ordering, every logical row/replay binding/checkpoint/Redis marker, and schema version remain unchanged. Initialization includes both in its existing transaction; writable open uses owner/health-fenced one-transaction DDL then rechecks health before returning a handle. Read-only/offline operations do not migrate. The owned startup task and blocking closure each retain the journal Arc through cancellation. Five real journal tests passed: populated legacy restart/export/token equality and query plans; first/latest membership and contradictory proof retention; readonly/owner/health gates; second-statement DDL rollback; deterministic caller and async-startup cancellation while an independent WAL writer blocks DDL. The migration stutters over DisasterRecovery logical state; SQLite DDL atomicity, real power loss, OS locks and Tokio cancellation remain implementation assumptions/tests, not new model theorems. No lookup-throughput improvement or bound on retained/per-ID history is claimed.

diagnostic_retention_followup.status: Applied formatted source independently reviewed; isolated eight-test Redis/serializer suite passed and both no-trim negative controls failed as intended. Full finite-model rerun recorded separately.
diagnostic_retention_followup.reason: All six single/multilane nack, failure and deserialization-failure append sites retain the same owner-fenced completion boundary and add newest-first LTRIM100. Metadata attempts, retry/backoff inputs, queue order/delay, lease state, hook pipeline, dedupe, cancellation and expiry operations do not change. Whole-tree reader review found no retry/protocol decision based on diagnostic cardinality; Solana orphan detection observes key existence, preserved by oversized-record omission markers. Bounded serialization preserves ordinary JobErrorRecord JSON, emits a distinct valid omission envelope above16KiB and preserves unrelated Serialize errors. Diagnostic inspection/size/order are outside QueueLease protocol variables, so these writes project to the same existing completion action (or stutter over diagnostic-only state); no new theorem or model/configuration is added. The model still assumes valid Redis key types and successful EXEC commands: Redis command errors may partially execute, and this patch does not strengthen that excluded failure boundary. Serializer byte bounds, TTL behavior, stale-owner append/trim rejection, attempt increments and legacy trim/turnover costs are implementation checks, not TLC proofs. External typed inspectors must recognize omission envelopes; legacy oversized entries age out, first large trim can be linear, and total/global retention remains outside the per-job cap.

dispatch_pipeline_followup.status: Final owned-Arc source reviewed after four intended negative-control failures, restored seven-send-test pass and formatting check. Full finite-model rerun recorded separately; previous evidence preserved.
dispatch_pipeline_followup.reason: Both new/recycled production paths first reserve signed borrowed wires as a batch, then authorize each wire in input order through immutable admission/wire validation and independent journal commit/mirror. Redis worker ownership is read on both sides of awaited authorization. One authorized network wait can overlap the next authorization; ordered bounded results retain ID association. First authorization error stops the producer; shared first-poll failure flag suppresses buffered unstarted sends, while already-started calls drain before returning that error. Entire batch remains borrowed on authorization error/cancellation; RPC errors remain Uncertain rather than terminal/recyclable. EoaRecovery already permits independent retained-identity Broadcast; DisasterRecovery permits authorized Send during later AttemptCommit/Mirror and late execution after halt/crash. Suppressed send is conservative non-delivery, not a new safety transition. Models do not represent whole-batch barriers, first-poll revocation, Tokio buffers/Arc/atomics, worker-owner reads, ordered responses, cancellation/draining mechanics, recycled preparation, concurrency/rate/fairness or throughput; no new theorem/configuration/refinement proof is claimed. Six new real Redis/SQLite/HTTP regressions verify these implementation cuts, including both actual entry points and real higher nonce4 around holes2/3. Four runtime mutations (whole-batch barrier, missing producer stop, missing post-owner fence, missing first-poll suppression) fail intended assertions/deadlines; compilation succeeds. A prior fixture with recycled nonces above highest submitted1 was correctly rejected by cleanup and repaired, not accepted as a runtime bug.
